summary: Package packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs. X6: applyLive takes its before-rendering from write.markdown when write.tree != nil (later operations), or from the room replica's markdown on a warm first operation when the replica's process-unique epoch and its count of non-liveWrite commits are unchanged between warmFork's counter read (before the encode) and replica.hold() after buildFork; otherwise it renders as today. X4: (A) a warm operation's after-markdown, plus askBlockIDs when contentChanged, rides its update's liveWriteOrigin with that fork read's epoch/foreign counters, and observe takes it when both still match; (B) an update whose version is <= the room instance's loadedHead (load.head) is already in the room, so observe classifies it unchanged without rendering (cold publishes, rooms reloaded before the publish); classify gets ask-block ids lazily; anything else renders as today. No ygo change; no markdown, tree or map outlives the transaction.
tasks: 1. Confirm with file:line in the PR: the loaded document holds every stored update through load.head; each publishLiveUpdate is exactly one room transaction with origin *liveWriteOrigin and nothing else uses that origin; settlement and identity repairs commit with other origins; warmFork's srv.Apply callback hands the resident document s.replicas is keyed by. A fact that fails drops its path, with the reason in the PR.

2. tree.go: renderedReplica epoch (from a package-level atomic, renewed on recover) and foreign (atomics, written under mu in commit order); classify gets lazy ask-block ids; websocket.go observeAskBlocksForUpdate takes the id set.

3. X6 (plan section 2.2): liveWrite.forkMarkdown, cleared at every forkLive and by dropRendering; warmFork records counters on every warm fork read; first-operation replica reuse; later-operation reuse of write.markdown; markdown = beforeMarkdown when unchanged.

4. X4 (plan section 2.3): write.renderings parallel to write.updates (warm only, zero entry when cold), copied from the counters right after forkLive at mutation.go:89; publishLiveUpdate carries the entry plus inRoom (version <= instance.loadedHead, read before hold.add) on the origin; observe paths (A) and (B); the origin's entry is cleared once observed; renderings nil at finishLiveWrite.

5. Tests E1-E13 of plan section 4 (shadow render check, path counters, a 400 KB generated document), negative controls breaking each guard, a throwaway real-LINUX-spec run (not committed), go test ./internal/dispatch/... and -race on ./internal/dispatch/docs/.

6. Docs: packages/envoy/AGENTS.md lines 311-316 and 774-779; doc comments tree.go:303-325,346-353,506-513, websocket.go:584-588, livewrite.go:79-88,136-146, mutation.go:109-113; packages/envoy/CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] Changed entry.

7. Measurement (plan section 5) at the head that merges, after the simplify pass: 3 base and 3 head runs of the architect's replay (or INFRA-639's when it lands), F=0.3, GOMAXPROCS=2, run/seeded.dump, one read action per write; the profile-share fallback with the stable foci; a throwaway hit-count build; the expected gain G stated before the head runs.
8. PR with 'Dispatch: INFRA-643', the equivalence evidence, runs, spread, commands, inputs, hit counts and E2E lines.

findings.finding: 1. The hint can match the wrong replica: a per-replica epoch restarts at zero, so a cold fork or a room evicted and reloaded before the publish could match a fresh replica.
findings.answer: Section 2.1: the epoch comes from one package-level atomic, so it is unique across replicas in the process, and is renewed on recover; cold forks carry no hint; counters are read from the replica of the doc srv.Apply hands warmFork. Tests E7, E8, E10.

findings.finding: 2. In the replay, rooms are mostly cold (1-minute idle eviction), so the warm hint and the first-operation replica reuse rarely fire.
findings.answer: Section 2.3 (B): an update whose version is <= the room instance's loadedHead is already in the room, so the observer classifies it unchanged without rendering; this covers cold publishes. A throwaway hit-count build measures each path's share on the replay (section 5).

findings.finding: 3. The spec's expected gain (0.13-0.23 cores) assumes X1-X3 landed, warm rooms and X3b, and its upper part is W13 (INFRA-644's).
findings.answer: Section 5: expected gain restated in percent of samples on the actual base, G from base shares and measured hit counts, stated before the head runs; W13 left to INFRA-644 (it would also keep a whole-document string resident for read-only rooms). Recorded as a spec departure.

findings.finding: 4. INFRA-642 (X3/X3b) overlaps: its origin tag, observe skip and ProjectMark changes.
findings.answer: Section 2.6: behaviour in either merge order stated; both ride liveWriteOrigin; the implementer gives INFRA-642's implementer the field names over Envoy; the second to merge adapts.

findings.finding: 5. The X6 fork-rendering field can go stale because buildFork drops only when write.tree != nil.
findings.answer: Section 2.2: forkMarkdown is cleared at the start of every forkLive, warm or cold, and set only when the check passes with len(write.updates)==0. Test E9.

findings.finding: 6. Counters must be paired with the operation's own fork read.
findings.answer: Section 2.3 (A): copied into a local right after forkLive at mutation.go:89, so no later fork read can overwrite them.

findings.finding: 7. Memory is not bounded or checked.
findings.answer: Section 2.5: renderings only for warm operations, equal markdowns share one string, the origin's entry is cleared once observed, renderings nil at finishLiveWrite; E13 extends cold_edit_test.go:63; inuse_space compared in the replay.

findings.finding: 8. Ask-block ids are an added walk; computing them eagerly in observe adds walks.
findings.answer: Section 2.4: lazy on the rendering path; computed in applyLive only when contentChanged (the observer stops walking for that update); render if the hint says changed but has no ids.

findings.finding: 9. The equivalence check is not machine-checkable as written; content_changed rows test X6, not X4.
findings.answer: Section 4: shadow render of the room against the replica markdown, askBlocks/askAuthors and each update's class; path counters prove each test exercised its path; negative controls; E4-E12 cover each fallback named.

findings.finding: 10. The merge-rule input does not exist yet and the W6 pprof focus (applyLive.func2) is unstable.
findings.answer: Section 5: the architect's replay tools and inputs per its 15:10Z instruction (INFRA-639's replay if it lands first); stable foci documentMarkdown$ under applyLive and updateChangesMarkdown$; thresholds in percent of samples.
Section 6 lists packages/envoy/AGENTS.md lines and each doc comment, plus a CHANGELOG entry.

specDepartures.spec: Outcome: 'the observer's [render] from the write's' (reuse the write's after-render for the observer).
specDepartures.plan: Also skips the observer render for an update already in the room (version <= the room instance's load head): the replica's existing rendering is of the same state. This is the cold-publish case, where the write's own rendering cannot be paired with the replica.
specDepartures.evidence: roomIdleTimeout is one minute (service.go:48-51); a write with no resident room cold-forks and its publish loads the room from a store that holds the write (livewrite.go:374-376); in the replay W10 cold fork 1.75% against W9 warm fork 0.58% (ranking rows), so path (A) alone would rarely fire.

specDepartures.spec: Acceptance: 'Expected: about 0.13-0.23 cores (X4 0.08-0.18, X6 0.05), estimated', the expected gain the merge rule's profile-share route uses.
specDepartures.plan: States the expected gain G in percent of profile samples on the base this merges onto, from the base profile's W6 and W12 shares and measured path hit counts, before the head runs. Leaves X4's start(base) part (up to 0.10, W13) to INFRA-644, as the spec's Overlap orders.
specDepartures.evidence: The ranking's X4 and X6 estimates are fractions of what X1+X2+X3 leave and assume X3b took margin-only updates (ranking X3b, X4, X6 removal lines); none of those is on main 59f6647d.

outcome.scope: The merge rule's expected gain is the measured G, not 0.13-0.23 cores; W13 (start(base) reusing the load's render) is not in this issue.
